title: Python: ALIAS-adjacent gaps shared with m.attr() and C.m() (GCLI-113 review item 2; item 1, the del gap, is GCLI-115)
description: Found in the GCLI-113 round 1 review. (1) The walker has no delete_statement arm: `del f` makes f local to its function in Python (so a nested `nonlocal f` is legal and a read of f is a local read), but no binding is recorded. Today the effect is that applyScopeRedirects falls back to the nearest enclosing function and a binding written by a nonlocal in a nested scope can be the only recorded binding of the local; ALIAS reads B at the binding's origin to stay correct. A del of the NAME is also not counted by enumerableBindings for 6d, R4, K1, LIT, M1 and ALIAS (e.g. `x = C(); del x; x = D()`-style sequences are unaffected because the other bindings are counted, but a name whose only binding is deleted and re-bound by a nonlocal write is not seen). Fix in the walker (record a del target as a binding kind that refuses every rule), with a refused fixture per rule, and a five-pin corpus diff that names any site that moves. (2) Gaps ALIAS shares with the direct m.attr() and C.m() resolution and does not widen, named for the same task: a package __init__ def shadowed by a submodule of the same name, Cls.attr = v or setattr(Cls, ...) from outside the module, metaclass descriptors, a decorated class, an opaque base before an in-repo def, rule 44 (type = m.func). Not in the DEC-303 build order; a follow-up. DEC-303 (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the shared gaps named in the description each get a fixture recording today behaviour (resolves or refuses) and a decision for the operator route if a fix is wanted
a per-site five-pin corpus diff is recorded and any site that moves is named

implementationNotes: Item 1 of this task (the del gap) is subsumed by GCLI-115, widened by DEC-303 (a40) item 1 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2006): a del target is a binding for scope purposes. Item 2 (the gaps ALIAS shares with m.attr() and C.m()) stays here.

Narrowed (DEC-303 (a45) item 3, GCLI-116 build PR): item 1, the del statement gap, landed under GCLI-115 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#180) and is no longer part of this task. Only item 2 remains: the gaps ALIAS shares with m.attr() and C.m(). Any remainder that changes a resolution comes to opum-doc before a build.

Reconciled against GCLI-115 and GCLI-116 (Done) and GCLI-118 (To Do), read on origin/dev 9e7a21b, 2026-11-26 (opum-doc request via leader). Not closed as superseded: item 1 (the del gap) is covered by GCLI-115 (#180), so AC 1 is removed here; GCLI-116's title and description and GCLI-118's carry none of item 2's gaps (package __init__ def shadowed by a submodule, Cls.attr = v or setattr(Cls, ...) from outside the module, metaclass descriptors, a decorated class, an opaque base before an in-repo def, rule 44 type = m.func), so item 2 remains and stays To Do, priority low. Remaining criteria: a fixture per named gap recording today's behaviour, and a five-pin corpus diff naming any site that moves. Any fix that changes a resolution, bin or flag comes to opum-doc before a build; nothing is built here.
